content:
maya: heads-up — we just started seeing a cluster of local-ssd devices remount as read-only in eu-central-1 (3 nodes so far). SMART shows spiking reallocated sectors. :frowning_face:

maya: ops-bot posted the alert at 2198765400, not sure if it's correlated with the big batch jobs that launched ~2198765200

ops-bot: [alert] node/gpu-worker-42: nvme_realloc_count > threshold (15) — auto-evict triggered

kai: can you paste the smart log? curious if it's reallocation or something else (firmware?).

maya: pasted quick output below:
```
sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
smart_log: critical_warning: 0
temperature: 42 C
available_spare: 100%
reallocated_sector_count: 1234
unsafe_shutdown_count: 4
media_errors: 5

Firmware Revision: 3.2.1
PCIe Link: gen3 x8
```

ezra: 1.2k reallocs is a lot — that can trigger internal ECC retries and slow IOs which will cascade when GPU batching pushes concurrent IO. saw this pattern last month with a different FW on spot pools.

liam: are these nodes on the shared scratch pool or dedicated scratch per pod? we should drain from the scheduler if they’re hitting media errors.

maya: shared scratch. right now we get tight IO bursts from inference-batching which explodes write amplification on small ephemeral files.

kai: +1 to drain. i'll open an incident and add a k8s taint to avoid new pods: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-worker-42 ssd-failing=true:NoSchedule`

sre-bot: runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/storage/reallocated-sectors — follow section B for safe evacuation.

ezra: quick mitigation I'd suggest: 1) throttle batch write concurrency in the inference worker (reduce -max-open-files / add jitter), 2) disable aggressive ephemeral GC on those nodes for now, 3) move critical jobs to dedicated disks in eu-west-1 if capacity allows.

liam: capacity in eu-west-1 is limited this week — we have ~2 reserved racks free but not enough GPU slots for all. we can temporarily switch lower-priority jobs. cost impact minimal if short.

maya: noted. starting evacuation on node 42 and 43, will mark 44 for monitoring. kai — please create incident with timeline and assign follow-ups.

kai: done — incident/2026-03-18-ssd-realloc created, assigning to @liam for capacity, @ezra for FW analysis, @maya for node remediation.

maya: FW note: these devices run 3.2.1. ezra, can you check vendor bulletins if 3.2.2 or 3.3.x fixed reallocation storm regressions?

ezra: checking now. vendor has a hotfix 3.2.3 that addresses reallocation spike under sustained small-block writes. will validate against backup node images.

sre-bot: suggestion: add SMART-based autoscale action to prevent scheduler from sending new IO-heavy jobs when reallocated_sector_count > 500. filing a proposal: https://redwood-internal/ops/proposals/smart-autoscale

liam: for immediate relief I can spin 2 dedicated scratch nodes in eu-west-1 and shift batch jobs flagged as high-write. will do in 15m.

maya: thanks. follow-ups list: (1) evacuate affected nodes (maya), (2) capacity ramp and job migration (liam), (3) firmware check and test image (ezra), (4) incident doc and RCA tracking (kai).

maya: quick note — we should throttle inference-batcher concurrency across the fleet until FW is confirmed; adding a global feature flag is fastest. :thumbsup:

kai: acknowledged, adding flag rollout to the incident playbook.

maya: ok closing loop for now — will post updates in the incident thread. :eyes:
